entityDescription:
CERMAT is a Polish SME specialising in advanced technical ceramics and precision surface finishing. The company manufactures and machines components from alumina (Al₂O₃), zirconia-toughened alumina (ZTA), zirconia (ZrO₂), silicon carbide (SiC) and sintered carbides, serving industrial customers across Poland and the EU.
Core competencies include precision lapping and polishing of ceramic components down to sub-micron flatness, diamond grinding, cutting-edge geometry for ceramic and carbide tools, and dimensional metrology to ISO 1101 (CMM-based flatness, parallelism and coaxiality verification). The company operates its own production and finishing facility, including flat lapping equipment for components up to 600 mm, and provides dye-penetrant inspection of ceramic parts.
The company additionally offers ceramic additive manufacturing (vat photopolymerisation / DLP) of alumina components, covering the full process chain from green-body printing through debinding and sintering to post-sinter precision grinding and lapping of functional surfaces — enabling complex geometries such as thin-walled (0.5 mm) monolithic parts, internal channels and near-net-shape components with machined datum surfaces.

entityDescription:
LoreSpace develops decision-support software for spacecraft systems engineering, based on a formal Space Systems Engineering Ontology in OWL/RDF aligned with ECSS practice and the spacecraft lifecycle (Phases A–F).
The system ingests programme artefacts — system and subsystem requirements, interface control documents, verification matrices, test and anomaly records — and connects them into a programme knowledge graph. Engineers query the graph in natural language and receive evidence-backed, cited answers; the system generates and maintains engineering artefacts from the same model, providing digital continuity across organisational and disciplinary boundaries in model-based system approaches.
Capabilities: ontology and knowledge-model development; requirements and verification traceability; automated change-impact and variant-delta analysis; configuration management support; document-to-graph ingestion pipelines; SPARQL/SHACL validation; agentic workflow automation over programme data.
LoreSpace AB is a Swedish company based in Stockholm, incubated at ESA BIC Sweden.

entityDescription:
Eckert & Ziegler Cesio manufactures sealed radioactive sources with Cs-137 and Co-60 emitting high-energy gamma radiation, Am-241 emitting low-energy gamma radiation and X-rays, Am-241/Be sources emitting neutron radiation, Kr-85 emitting beta radiation and foil radioactive sources with Am-241 emitting alpha particles.
Sealed radioactive sources with Cs-137 and Co-60 are primarily used as high-energy gamma sources in level gauges and material thickness measuring gauges in industrial plants, some models of Cs-137 sources are designed for use in well logging applications.
Sealed sources containing Am-241 are applied in X-ray fluorescence analysis of materials. Especially suitable for this purpose are Am-241 radioactive sources with an output window made of Beryllium enabling the emission of X-rays and low-energy gamma radiation. Low-energy gamma radiation of Am-241 is used in level gauges for scanning of the content of small objects, such as beverage cans and bottles, and also in thickness measuring gauges, as it allows to measure materials with lower area density compared to gauges fitted with Cs-137 and Co-60 sources.
Neutron radiation of radioactive sources with Am-241/Be is used for oil well logging, calibration of neutron measuring devices, as well as for determination of moisture in soil and in building materials in agriculture and construction industry, respectively. Am-241/Be sources also find use in education and research projects at universities.
Radioactive sources with Kr-85 are suitable particularly for beta thickness gauging, including measurement of very thin materials such as plastic, thin metal sheets, textiles and rubber. The emission of beta radiation is enabled through a specially designed thin output window with the thickness of 0.025 mm or 0.05 mm.
Foil radioactive sources with Am-241 contain americium homogeneously dispersed in gold mounted on a silver backing. Alpha particles are emitted from the source surface through a front cover made of gold or gold-palladium alloy. Foil sources are used in smoke detectors and in electrostatic charge eliminators.

description:
Vulcanis SAS is a French deep-tech SME, founded in 2025 and based in Paris, developing integrated optical sensing instruments for the in-situ characterisation of geological materials. Our core technology fuses shortwave-infrared hyperspectral imaging (HSI), standoff laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) and LiDAR into a single co-registered instrument governed by physics-constrained edge AI executing onboard. The architecture is cue-and-confirm: the dense passive hyperspectral scene identifies candidate targets and directs a limited budget of active LIBS acquisitions, whose elemental ground truth is then propagated back across the LiDAR-co-registered scene. The output is a georeferenced mineralogical and elemental map delivered within the same working shift, in place of the multi-day sampling and laboratory assay cycle it replaces. Standoff LIBS is engineered around a 20–30 m working envelope.

Related activities: instrument architecture and optical design; LIBS and hyperspectral spectroscopy; multi-sensor calibration, co-registration and spectral data fusion; and physics-constrained machine learning for autonomous onboard analysis. The primary terrestrial application is grade control and tailings characterisation for the mining industry; the same sensing stack addresses planetary surface prospecting and ISRU site characterisation. Current maturity is TRL 4.

Vulcanis holds a signed memorandum of understanding with Exploration Labs (EXlabs) on instrument accommodation for future deep-space missions, and is incubated at Télécom Paris / Institut Polytechnique de Paris. The team combines planetary-instrument science with two decades of industrial computer-vision engineering.
entityDescription:
Vulcanis SAS is a French deep-tech SME headquartered in Paris, France, incorporated as a Société par Actions Simplifiée under French law. The company designs and develops modular multi-sensor payloads for real-time, in-situ mineralogical characterization, with applications spanning terrestrial critical raw materials exploration and planetary surface prospecting.
Vulcanis's core technology is the Vulcanis Mapping Payload (VMP), a sensor-fusion instrument integrating Shortwave Infrared (SWIR) Hyperspectral Imaging (900–2500 nm), Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS), LiDAR, and physics-constrained edge AI on NVIDIA Jetson-class compute. The architecture fuses dense passive hyperspectral data with sparse active LIBS sampling, co-registered through LiDAR, to deliver real-time mineral classification and ore grade estimation without lab turnaround.
For space applications, Vulcanis is developing VMP-Lunar, an instrument variant for in-situ mineralogical prospecting of lunar regolith and pyroclastic deposits in support of In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) objectives. The lunar variant targets a 10–14 kg mass envelope, 40–60 W nominal power, and aligns with NASA Moon-to-Mars objective AS-03.

entityDescription: SpectrAl SAS is a French company founded in August 2025 by Gabriel Hmimina, an engineer with extensive experience in ecophysiology and remote sensing. Our core activities include low‑cost sensor networks for soil, air, and vegetation monitoring, as well as advanced satellite‑based methods for assessing ecosystem phenology and physiology. By early 2026, we had prototyped connected soil moisture, air temperature/humidity, and PAR sensors and deployed a dedicated local data‑processing server.
